body.statement: What is the sharp local envelope of \(\omega^{\star}(\delta)-\omega^{\star}(0)\) as \(\delta\downarrow0\), and which observable prefix-Gram restrictions identify subclasses on which the restricted modulus vanishes? Use the annulus decomposition of \(\psi_{n,k}-\psi_{n,l}\) and the explicit tied-risk witness to derive matching upper and lower bounds without imposing an oracle restriction on candidate bias.
body.justification: The counterexample settles the global exact-tie question negatively but leaves the sharp excess modulus and the largest empirically meaningful benign-tie subclass open.
body.gap: No located paper gives a risk-to-target modulus for generated external-control prefixes or a prefix-Gram restriction that restores tie invariance.
body.consumer: The sharp envelope determines how much a localized confidence interval must widen beyond its unavoidable exact-tie width.
